candidates: When adding internal cross-page links in documentation, use `.md` extensions (e.g., `../ecosystem/mermaid-chart.md`) rather than `.html` extensions. VitePress resolves `.md` links automatically in the rendered site, and `.html` links break when the markdown is read outside the rendered site.

When adding same-page anchor links, use bare fragment references (e.g., `#_1-using-the-live-editor`) rather than prefixing the current filename (e.g., `getting-started.md#_1-using-the-live-editor`). The filename prefix creates a broken link when the page is rendered.

In Markdown numbered lists, write the correct sequential numbers in the raw source (1, 2, 3, …) rather than repeating `1.` for every item. Although most renderers auto-correct the output, readers of the raw source file rely on the numbers written in the file being accurate.

When linking to third-party tools or services, prefer official canonical documentation URLs over internal handbook or secondary pages. For example, use `https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/markdown.html#mermaid` instead of a GitLab handbook URL for GitLab's Mermaid support.

The `docs/` directory is auto-generated from `packages/mermaid/src/docs/`; the files carry a header warning against direct edits. When a PR edits both the source tree and the generated `docs/` tree, verify that the generated files are fully in sync with the source and check the generated output for broken links.
